Migrate wizard — the connect step’s already-installed accounts: account list, sign-in prompt, repository picker and every link outcome · delta of onboarding-migrate--connect-states.mock.html (MOTIR-8758 · Revision 8)

Index · the connect step’s already-installed-account panels — card state # → board panel id (2a–2k as drawn; 2l–2t are new)

Revision 7 numbers the connect step’s panels 2a–2k (onboarding-migrate--connect-states.mock.html) and that numbering governs. These panels continue it as 2l–2t, one letter per state on MOTIR-8758, with roman sub-panels for its variants. No existing id changes meaning.

Only the card body changes. The rail and StepHead are as drawn in the predecessors; each frame shows the work band only. Each panel draws light and dark.

GitHub-side hrefs are fragments naming their builder (lib/github/appLinks.ts): #githubAppInstallUrl(state), #githubInstallationManageUrl(installation). The sample logins and repository names are placeholders.

card state # panels state its next action
1 2l.i · 2l.ii Account list, populated (1 · 3, mixed) pick an account
2 2m.i · 2m.ii Account list loading · could not check none · Try again
3 2n No accounts → pre-flight (2b) unchanged Connect GitHub
4 2o.i–iv Identity prompt: default · in flight · back · declined Sign in with GitHub · skip
5 2p.i–iv Picker: row kinds · loading · error · 50+ Connect N
6 2q Nothing left to offer Choose another account
7 2r.i · 2r.ii select_repos arrival · unreachable Connect N · pick another account
8 2s.i–vii Linked · taken · 422 guard · 422 not visible · 403 ×2 · not an admin per panel
9 2t.i–iii With already connected · owner pending · cancelled Continue · pick an account

2l.i · Account list, populated — one account (card #1) — light | dark · 1280 px

When it holds — the accounts read answers ok with one account, and no installation is bound to this organisation yet.

Its one next action — pick the account row; the picker (2p) opens for it in place. The install row below starts the predecessor’s install (2e → 2c), unchanged.

Data — per account: login, type (GitHub organisation / personal account), avatar (initial disc when none), link state (already linked here / not linked).

Step 1 of 2 · Set up

Connect the repositories in this project

Motir reads the repositories you connect on GitHub and builds one map of the code across the project.

You connect GitHub, then come straight back

GitHub opens in a new tab for about a minute. This is what happens there, and this step is waiting when you come back.

  1. 1

    Choose the GitHub account to install the Motir GitHub App on: your own account, or a GitHub organisation you belong to.

  2. 2

    Choose all repositories, or only the ones you select. You can change this later on GitHub.

  3. 3

    Approve the access the App asks for. It can read and change code and pull requests, and read checks, deployments, issues, merge queues, metadata and security events.

GitHub sends you straight back to this step, and it shows the repositories you connected.

GitLab connect is coming soon.

2o.i · Identity prompt — default (card #4) — light | dark · 1280 px

When it holds — the accounts read answers identity_required: Motir has no GitHub sign-in for this person, so it cannot ask GitHub which installations they can reach.

One primary (Sign in with GitHub, warm) and one skip (quiet link). Skip removes the prompt and leaves the predecessor’s pre-flight (2b). The install row stays under the prompt, so the install path never depends on signing in.

Opened by picking an account (2l) or by the select_repos return (2r). It replaces the list inside the card; Back to accounts goes back.

Rows are MOTIR-8217’s: available (selectable), connected to another organisation (disabled, lock, never names who), connected here (checked, locked, labelled). Counter and Connect N in the card’s footer row; Connect is disabled at 0.

Data — per repository: full name, availability. The account’s login names the header.
